title: header-truncation-causes-anonymous-rate-limit-surge-and-soft-429s
creator: Aisha Patel
summary: A subset of requests had their X-Client-ID header truncated at the ingress layer after a recent proxy change, causing the gateway to classify them as anonymous and drive an unexpected spike of 429s under the anonymous quota policy.
incident_description: On 2026-03-01 we observed a sustained increase in 429 responses from the API gateway that correlated with a spike in 'anonymous' bucket usage. The surge began at ~03:12 UTC and persisted for ~2 hours until mitigations were applied. The event affected a variety of customers intermittently; downstream services remained healthy but client retries amplified the load and increased latency for some high-throughput clients.
impact_summary: Peak anonymous 429 rate reached ~9% of total gateway responses during the incident window. Several medium-traffic customers reported degraded request success rates; automated healthchecks and ingestion pipelines saw transient failures. No data loss was reported. Estimated customer ROI impact: degraded feature availability and increased retry cost.
detection: Alerting triggered from the SLO dashboard (5xx/429 ratio) and custom metric 'gateway.anonymous_quota.usage' which showed a 4x baseline bump. On-call engineer correlated the 429 spike with a near-simultaneous increase in requests missing X-Client-ID in request traces.
timeline: 2026-03-01T03:09:00Z - Low-level uptick in 429s begins; early alerts not triggered
2026-03-01T03:12:42Z - SLO alert fires for 429 ratio; on-call paged
2026-03-01T03:20:00Z - Initial triage: majority of 429s mapped to anonymous quota enforcement
2026-03-01T03:28:00Z - Investigation finds many ingress logs with X-Client-ID length >64 bytes were recorded as empty after proxy trimming
2026-03-01T03:35:00Z - Temporary mitigation: increase anonymous quota threshold and enable short-circuit accept for known VIP IP ranges
2026-03-01T04:05:00Z - Deploy rollback of the proxy change that introduced header truncation; monitored metrics begin to normalize
2026-03-01T05:20:00Z - 429 rates back within baseline; mitigation validated; follow-up items created
root_cause: Two factors converged: a) a rolling change to the edge proxy (envoy config) limited header buffer size to 64 bytes for performance reasons, and b) a recent SDK change made X-Client-ID values substantially longer (unique tenant+session payload). When the header exceeded the buffer, the proxy silently truncated it, and our gateway auth layer treated missing/empty X-Client-ID as 'anonymous', which is subject to a strict global quota. The system lacked a clear metric for 'header-dropped' and the ingress returned 200 for the truncated request so downstream observability didn't surface header-size rejections.
immediate_mitigation: Rolled back the proxy config change within 30 minutes, temporarily increased the anonymous quota caps for affected regions, and added a diagnostic flag to the ingress to log truncated-header events to a dedicated metric stream. Customer-facing retries were throttled at the gateway to reduce amplification.
longer_term_fix_summary: Fixes include updating the ingress to explicitly return 431 on header-too-large, increasing header buffer defaults safely, adding an assertion in the auth layer to reject empty X-Client-ID instead of treating as anonymous, and updating the SDK to shorten the client identifier encoding. We will also add end-to-end regression tests that exercise long header scenarios and add a synthetic check to the SLO dashboard for header-preservation.

notes: This incident highlights a recurring class of failures where transport-layer changes silently mutate metadata we rely on for quota routing. We should consider a small compatibility test harness that runs on any proxy/ingress change and validates header fidelity for critical headers.

verification_plan: After fixes, verify with the following: 1) run synthetic long-header sweep across regions for 48h, 2) confirm no 431/400 regressions for normal traffic, 3) validate anonymous quota and X-Client-ID mapping metrics are stable for one production cycle.
closing_notes: Core mitigations completed and monitoring added. Remaining action items prioritized for the next two sprints; will track completion in gateway-reliability project board. No further customer credits expected at this time.
